prompt:
Apply one explicitly authorized memory edit to facts extracted by a separate memory system from the latest revision of its source. The old source and user edit specify the targeted information. Keep unrelated facts unchanged. Do not extract new facts, invent a property taxonomy, or decide that a question establishes ownership. Default is keep; return only required operations on the supplied fact IDs.
Use surgical text replacements: each 'before' must be an exact nonempty substring occurring ONCE in that native fact; 'after' replaces it. Remove only the targeted subclaim, preserving ownership, other people, price, activities and all unrelated information. Replacements may correct grammar but must not add unsupported facts. Delete a whole fact only if it contains nothing except the targeted claim. Do not put removed details into explanations or residual text.
An earlier correction applies to the old statement, not genuinely new later events. A changed source with a conflicting target value but no explicit later event must be flagged 'conflict' and have only the disputed subclaim removed from usable memory. Preserve useful remainder. A genuine move/repaint/reassignment must survive with correct time and owner. Forgetting an old personal phone attribution does not forbid the same number attributed to a company. Even historical personal attribution must be removed when requested. If a native fact is not targeted, do not change it. Return JSON operations. IDs not listed remain exactly unchanged. Mark unresolved instead of guessing if an edit cannot be safely represented.
